login.title: Sign in
login.sub: Sign in to manage mail flow, quarantine and settings.
login.forgot: Forgot your password? Ask your administrator to set a new one.

info.title: About Mailfilter
info.updates_soon: Checking for and installing updates from here is coming in the next release.

dashboard.title: Dashboard
dashboard.sub_admin: Everything that went through the gateway. Mail trace and quarantine are filled as soon as mail flows.
dashboard.next_users: Add users and link customers to their domains
dashboard.next_trace: Search any message in Mail trace
dashboard.next_quarantine: Release or block messages in Quarantine
dashboard.next_dns: Connect Cloudflare and check your domains' DNS

account.title: My account
account.name: Name
account.mismatch: The new passwords are not the same.
account.changed: Password changed. Other sessions were logged out.

users.title: Users
users.sub: Admins manage everything. Customers only see mail for the domains linked to them.
users.name: Name
users.password_hint: Leave empty to generate one. At least 10 characters.
users.password_keep: Leave empty to keep the current password.
users.generated: User created. Give them this password; it is shown only once:
users.delete_confirm: Delete {{email}}? They can no longer sign in.
users.domains_hint: Customers only see mail from and to these domains.
users.no_domains: No domains yet. Add domains under Domains first.

dns.title: DNS toolbox
dns.sub: Check a domain's mail DNS, generate SPF and DMARC, publish straight to Cloudflare and switch domains over to Mailfilter.
dns.not_managed: {{domain}} is not a domain in Mailfilter yet, so going live is not possible. Add it under Domains first.

publish_help.spf: Your current SPF value stays as it is; Mailfilter only adds itself. Nothing else changes.
publish_help.spf_value: This replaces the domain's SPF record with the generated value.
publish_help.dkim: Publishes the public key Mailfilter signs outbound mail with.
publish_help.dmarc: This sets the domain's DMARC record to the value shown.
publish_help.server_spf: The shared record that lists all Mailfilter addresses. Domains include this name.

problem.syntax: The record has a syntax error.
problem.multiple_spf: The domain has more than one SPF record; receivers treat that as an error. Remove all but one.
problem.no_all: The record has no "all" at the end.
problem.plus_all: "+all" allows the whole internet to send for this domain.
problem.ptr_deprecated: The "ptr" mechanism is deprecated and slow.
problem.long: The record is very long; consider an include.
problem.mailfilter_missing: Mailfilter is not in the SPF record yet, so outbound mail through Mailfilter may fail SPF.
problem.too_many_lookups: More than 10 DNS lookups: SPF fails at receivers.
problem.too_many_void_lookups: More than 2 lookups that find nothing.
problem.policy_none: Policy "none" only monitors; spoofed mail is still delivered.
problem.pct_partial: The policy applies to only part of the mail.
problem.mismatch: The DNS record does not match the key in Mailfilter.
problem.revoked: The key in DNS is revoked (empty p=).
problem.no_key: Mailfilter has no DKIM key for this domain.
problem.mx_mixed: MX points partly to Mailfilter and partly elsewhere.
problem.mx_elsewhere: MX does not point to Mailfilter yet.
problem.ptr: No matching PTR record for {{value}}. Ask your hosting provider to set it to the Mailfilter host name.

note.null_mx: The domain says it accepts no mail at all (null MX).
note.no_mx: No MX record; mail goes to the A/AAAA record of {{host}}.
note.no_address: {{host}} has no IPv4 or IPv6 address.
note.no_starttls: {{host}} has no STARTTLS. Mail to it travels unencrypted.
note.cert_name: The certificate of {{host}} is for another name.

mx.help: Look up where mail for any domain goes, for example a customer's: addresses, reverse DNS, port 25 and STARTTLS.
mx.ph: Any domain, for example a customer's
mx.probe: Also test port 25 and STARTTLS (takes a few seconds)
mx.null_mx: This domain accepts no mail (null MX).

spf.help: Build an SPF record and publish it straight to Cloudflare.
spf.merge_title: Add Mailfilter to an existing SPF
spf.merge_help: Use Check domain and "Publish to Cloudflare" next to SPF: your current value stays and Mailfilter only adds itself.

dmarc.help: Build a DMARC record. Start with "none" to collect reports, then move to quarantine and reject.
dmarc.policy_none: Receivers deliver everything and send you reports.
dmarc.policy_quarantine: Mail that fails goes to the receiver's spam folder.

bl.help: Mailfilter checks its own IPv4 and IPv6 addresses against the major blocklists every 15 minutes.
bl.none_yet: No check has run yet. Click "Check now".
bl.unusable: These lists did not answer their own test entry from this server, so their result is not known: {{lists}}.

cf.title: Cloudflare connection
cf.help: With an API token Mailfilter can publish SPF, DKIM and DMARC and switch MX records for you. Every change is shown first and can be undone.
cf.token_hint: In Cloudflare: My Profile, API Tokens, Create Token. Permissions: Zone: Read and DNS: Edit, for the zones Mailfilter may change. Stored encrypted.
cf.remove_confirm: Remove the Cloudflare token from Mailfilter?
cf.server_spf_help: Publishes {{name}} with all addresses of this server. Domains only include this name, so adding a server later changes one record.

gl.title: Go live
gl.help: One-time switch for this domain: points the MX record in Cloudflare to {{host}}. Mailfilter checks everything first and keeps the old value so you can roll back.

c.accepts: Mailfilter accepts mail for this domain

gl.force: Go live anyway, even though checks failed
gl.done_toast: Live: MX now points to Mailfilter
gl.rollback_confirm: Put the previous MX records back? Mail will go to the old server again.
gl.rolled_back: Rolled back: the previous MX records are back
gl.was_rolled_back: This domain was rolled back earlier. You can go live again.

log.help: Every change Mailfilter made in Cloudflare, with the old value. Undo puts the old value back. Go-live is undone with Roll back on the domain.
log.undo_confirm: Put the old value back in Cloudflare?

alert.title: Mailfilter is on a blocklist
alert.detail: {{ip}} is listed on {{name}} ({{zone}}) since {{time}}. Outbound mail to some providers may be refused. Check outbound spam, then request removal.
alert.customer: Outbound mail to some providers may be refused for a while. We are working on it.
